outcome: No resolution, case, or bound-moving result specific to the Birch-Tate conjecture (relating #K2(O_F) to ζ_F(-1) for totally real F) was found in the window; only a formalization request with no proof content, and adjacent/generalizing work on the broader Quillen-Lichtenbaum framework and on tame kernels, neither of which addresses this conjecture directly.
summary: No result settling any case of, or moving a bound within, the Birch-Tate conjecture as stated (the equality/near-equality of #K2(O_F) to |ζ_F(-1)| up to powers of 2, for a totally real number field F) was found for the period 26 January 2024 to 22 September 2026. The conjecture was already known up to a power of 2 (Wiles's theorem on the Iwasawa Main Conjecture, plus Kolster's remark handling the 2-part for abelian fields) well before the window, and nothing in this window closes the remaining 2-primary gap or extends the abelian case to full generality. The closest candidate, Elmanto-Zhang's 'Equivariant algebraic K-theory and Artin L-functions' (arXiv:2405.03578, submitted 6 May 2024), generalizes the Quillen-Lichtenbaum conjecture (a related but distinct statement, itself a source of Birch-Tate-adjacent results) to Artin L-functions of Galois representations, proving cases integrally except up to powers of 2 in the non-abelian/totally real case — but its abstract and introduction do not mention the Birch-Tate conjecture, and its scope (general Artin L-functions with coefficients in Galois representations) is a different, broader statement, not a restriction of Birch-Tate's specific claim about ζ_F(-1) and K2(O_F). Under §3.1 this is a related problem, not a case, so it does not count as a change to this bullet. A second candidate, arXiv:2308.04099 (Lim, 'On the p-divisibility of even K-groups...', v1 August 2023, v3 corrections uploaded 5 August 2025, published in Ramanujan Journal 2025) predates the window in its substantive content (v1 2023) and in any case does not mention Birch-Tate in its abstract; its 2025 revision is corrections/rewriting, not new mathematical content within the window, so this is at most open_stale-adjacent noise and does not change the status. A third candidate, arXiv:2504.15767 ('Is there a Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer conjecture for Dedekind zeta functions?', submitted 22 April 2025) is explicitly about an analogue of BSD for Dedekind zeta functions of number fields, a different question from Birch-Tate's K2 statement, and does not address Birch-Tate. Only one item was found that names the Birch-Tate conjecture directly within the window: a Google DeepMind 'formal-conjectures' GitHub issue (#1764, opened 18 January 2026) requesting Lean formalization of the Birch-Tate conjecture statement, tagged 'needs-prerequisites' because algebraic K-theory foundations are not yet built in that library. It contains no proof attempt, no claimed progress, and no AI-generated content — it is a formalization backlog item with zero comments. This is not a mathematical result and does not move the status; it is noted only because it is the sole hit naming this conjecture in the window. Overall: status remains open, no_change_found true, and there is no AI involvement of any kind (ai_role none) since no AI system produced any mathematics, bound, or even a formalization attempt for this specific conjecture in the window.
competing_reading: If a future reader considered the Elmanto-Zhang generalization of Quillen-Lichtenbaum to Artin L-functions as 'progress adjacent to Birch-Tate' worth noting even though out of strict scope, one could argue for `progress` with a null direction; I judged this a related/variant problem under §3.1 (a different, broader statement about general Artin L-functions and Galois-equivariant K-groups, not a restriction of the totally-real-field, trivial-representation Dedekind zeta statement that is Birch-Tate), so I kept status at `open`.
what_would_settle_it: A paper or preprint within the window that explicitly proves or narrows the 2-primary gap in the Birch-Tate equality #K2(O_F) = |ζ_F(-1)| · #K3(O_F) (up to sign/normalization) for totally real F, or extends the abelian-field case (already known via Mazur-Wiles) to a genuinely new class of fields, citing Birch-Tate by name.
